explanation: erdosproblems.com/551: Keevash–Long–Skokan proved R(C_k, K_n) = (k−1)(n−1)+1 whenever k ≥ C log n / log log n, 'thus establishing the conjecture for sufficiently large n'. The Lean statement: for all sufficiently large n and every k ≥ n, graphRamsey (cycleGraph k) (K_n) = (k−1)(n−1)+1. For large n, k ≥ n implies k ≥ C log n / log log n, so this follows from KLS21; cycleGraph k for k ≥ n ≥ 3 is the genuine k-cycle, and graphRamsey is the standard two-graph Ramsey number. Faithful.
